stem:
Mona compares the calendar for year $Y$ with the calendar for year $Z$. She wants to know when year $Y$'s calendar can be reused for year $Z$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Reuse year $Y$'s calendar for year $Z$ after checking that only one special date (such as $1$ January) falls on the same weekday, without checking every date in the year.
Also treat a match of weekdays alone as settling whether two different month-name lists are the same calendar, beyond comparing dates and weekdays for years $Y$ and $Z$.
Reuse year $Y$'s calendar for year $Z$ only when every date in year $Z$ falls on the same weekday as that date in year $Y$.
Say the calendars match only because the printed year numbers $Y$ and $Z$ look alike, without comparing dates and weekdays.

teacher.key_rationale: A calendar repeats for another year only when every date keeps the same weekday. Matching one special date, stretching the test to unrelated month-name lists, or grabbing printed year numbers all miss that hinge.
